title: Best LLMrefs Alternatives (2026): Honest Picks for AI Visibility Tracking
metaDescription: The best LLMrefs alternatives in 2026, compared fairly: prompt-level data, freshness, price, and engine coverage — with AEOeye's free, instant multi-engine
shortAnswer: The best LLMrefs alternatives in 2026 are AEOeye (free, instant, blind multi-engine audit that shows the actual AI answers), Otterly.ai (low-cost prompt monitoring from $29/mo), Peec AI (fast mid-market tracking from €89/mo), Profound (enterprise depth around $499/mo), and Nightwatch (SEO rank tracking plus an AI add-on). LLMrefs is genuinely affordable at $79/mo, but people switch mainly for prompt-level visibility into why they appear, fresher data, and looser limits than its 1-keyword free plan allows.
intro:
LLMrefs does one thing well: it puts AI search visibility tracking within reach at $79/month, covering 11+ engines with keyword-style 'share of voice' scores that feel familiar to anyone coming from SEO. For a solo marketer or a small team just starting to treat AI mentions as a KPI, that's a reasonable on-ramp.

But 'familiar' cuts both ways. The same keyword-first framing that makes LLMrefs easy to read is what sends a lot of buyers looking for an alternative — they want to see the actual answer ChatGPT or Perplexity gave, which prompt triggered a citation, and what content won it, not just a number that went up or down. Add weekly-to-monthly refreshes, a 1-keyword free plan, and a Pro price labeled 'limited time only,' and the questions start. Below, we break down exactly why people leave LLMrefs — fairly, including where it's actually fine — and the best alternatives, starting with AEOeye's free instant audit.

sections.heading: Keyword-level scores, but no prompt-level visibility
sections.body:
LLMrefs aggregates results into keyword-level 'share of voice' rather than showing you the raw AI answer and the specific prompt that triggered a mention or citation. That design choice is the single most common reason people look elsewhere.

The problem is diagnostic. When your score drops, a keyword-level number tells you *that* something changed, not *why*. You can't see that Perplexity started citing a competitor's comparison page, or that ChatGPT paraphrased a Reddit thread instead of your docs. The independent GenerateMore review scored LLMrefs 2/5 on data accuracy and noted that it leans on 'traditional SEO terms to simplify AI SEO concepts,' which obscures how the models actually behave. It also flagged that the most actionable view — the Sources tab — is buried inside a simplified UX, so the data you'd act on takes digging to reach.

If your goal is to fix visibility, not just monitor it, you need the answer itself. AEOeye takes the opposite approach: it shows the real responses from each engine, names the brands the model recommended, and surfaces which competitors won — so you can see the cause, not just the symptom.

sections.heading: Data freshness that can lag for fast-moving categories
sections.body:
LLMrefs defaults to weekly refreshes, with monthly common on lighter usage and daily available but requiring configuration. For a slow, stable category that may be plenty. For anything competitive or fast-moving, reviewers consider it slow — GenerateMore scored freshness 2/5 and called it slower than most rivals.

There's a second, subtler reliability issue worth naming honestly: AI providers periodically change how responses are formatted, and citation parsers built on the old format can break until they're updated. When OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google shift their output, any tracker relying on parsing can show gaps for a stretch — and LLMrefs has been reported to be affected. This isn't unique to LLMrefs; it's a structural risk for every tool in this space. But it matters more when refreshes are infrequent, because a missed window plus a parser hiccup can leave you blind right when a trend is breaking. If you're publishing weekly and need to see the effect of a content change quickly, slower cadence is a real constraint — and a common trigger for switching to a tool that re-queries on demand.

sections.heading: Restrictive limits and a 'limited time only' price
sections.body:
Two pricing realities push people to compare. First, the free plan tracks just one keyword — useful for kicking the tires, not for actually running a program, so in practice it's a demo rather than a usable free tier. Second, there's a single 'All in One' Pro plan at $79/month capping you at 50 keywords and 500 prompts, limits reviewers describe as tight once you scale past a handful of topics or want to track competitors in depth.

To be fair, $79/mo is genuinely the low end of the paid market, and for many SMBs the caps are fine. But the Pro price is publicly labeled 'limited time only,' which is a fair warning to treat it as promotional rather than a locked-in, permanent rate when you're budgeting for a year. If you want to start at zero with no keyword cap on the audit itself, AEOeye's free instant audit runs your brand through real engines without asking you to pick a single keyword first. And if you outgrow LLMrefs' caps, the alternatives below scale in different directions — Otterly cheaply, Peec quickly, Profound deeply.

sections.heading: AEOeye — free, instant, blind multi-engine audit
sections.body:
AEOeye leads this list because it removes the two biggest frictions: cost and waiting. The audit is free to start and runs instantly — no sales call, no contract, no credit card to see your first result.

What it does: it asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini the questions real buyers actually type, then shows whether each engine recommends your brand, where you rank in the answer, and which competitors get named instead. Crucially, it's *blind* multi-engine querying — you see the real answers across engines side by side, which is exactly the prompt-level visibility LLMrefs' keyword scores abstract away. For a non-expert, that's the difference between a dashboard you stare at and an answer you can act on this afternoon.

Be clear on the trade-off, though. AEOeye is newer and deliberately lighter on enterprise analytics and long historical dashboards than incumbents like Profound; its deeper, continuous multi-engine querying activates with usage rather than being front-loaded into a heavy onboarding. If you need years of trended share-of-voice charts and SSO-gated team analytics on day one, a heavier platform fits better. If you want to know — right now, for free — whether AI recommends you or your competitor, start with AEOeye.

sections.heading: Otterly, Peec, Profound, and Nightwatch — fair comparisons
sections.body:
Four other real tools are worth a look depending on budget and depth.

**Otterly.ai** is the budget-friendly prompt monitor, with a Lite plan at $29/month (around 15 prompts), Standard at $189, and Premium at $489. It tracks brand mentions and citations across the major engines and now ships a public API and MCP server. Best for: cost-conscious teams that want prompt-level monitoring without enterprise pricing.

**Peec AI** targets the mid-market, starting near €89/month (about 25 prompts) with Pro around €199/month (100 prompts). Reviewers praise its speed and clean UX over exhaustive feature lists; it has raised significant funding and grown fast. Best for: teams that value usability and quick iteration.

**Profound** is the enterprise option at roughly $499/month for Lite, with Fortune 500 clients, deep analytics, and the historical dashboards AEOeye intentionally keeps light. It's the most expensive here and overkill for a solo marketer — but genuinely strong if you need depth and scale. Best for: large brands and agencies with budget.

**Nightwatch** comes at AI visibility from the SEO side: traditional rank tracking from about $32/month, plus an AI tracking add-on (~$99/month) so combined plans land near $131/month. It pairs Google/Bing/Maps rankings with AI Share of Voice, includes unlimited seats and white-label reports. Best for: SEO teams that want one tool for both rankings and AI citations.

keyTakeaways: LLMrefs is genuinely affordable ($79/mo, 11+ engines) and a fine on-ramp for SMBs — most people leave for prompt-level depth, fresher data, or looser limits, not because it's bad.

The core gap: LLMrefs reports keyword-level 'share of voice' instead of the actual AI answer and the prompt that triggered a citation, so it's hard to diagnose why you appear (GenerateMore scored it 2/5 on accuracy).

Data refreshes default to weekly (monthly common, daily requires setup), which reviewers call slow for fast-moving categories — and parser changes from OpenAI/Anthropic/Google can cause temporary gaps.
Limits feel tight: the free plan tracks just 1 keyword, Pro caps at 50 keywords / 500 prompts, and the $79 price is publicly labeled 'limited time only.'

AEOeye is the free, instant alternative — a blind multi-engine audit (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, Gemini) that shows the real answers and which competitors win, though it's lighter on enterprise historical dashboards.

Pick by need: Otterly (~$29/mo) for cheap prompt monitoring, Peec (~€89/mo) for fast mid-market UX, Profound (~$499/mo) for enterprise depth, Nightwatch (~$131/mo combined) to pair SEO rankings with AI visibility.

faqs.q: Is LLMrefs bad? Why would I switch?
faqs.a: LLMrefs isn't bad — at $79/month covering 11+ engines, it's one of the most affordable AI visibility trackers and a reasonable starting point for small teams. People switch for specific reasons: they want prompt-level visibility (the actual AI answer and the prompt that triggered a citation) rather than keyword-level 'share of voice' scores; they need fresher data than the default weekly-to-monthly refresh; or they hit the limits — a 1-keyword free plan and a 50-keyword/500-prompt Pro cap. If those don't bother you, LLMrefs may be fine as-is.

faqs.q: What's the best free alternative to LLMrefs?
faqs.a: AEOeye is the strongest free option. LLMrefs' free plan only tracks one keyword, which makes it a demo rather than a usable tier. AEOeye's audit is free to start and runs instantly — no sales call or contract — and queries ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude, and Gemini with the questions real buyers ask, then shows whether each recommends your brand, where you rank, and which competitors win. The trade-off is that AEOeye is lighter on long historical dashboards than paid incumbents; its deeper multi-engine querying activates with usage.

faqs.q: Why does prompt-level data matter more than keyword-level scores?
faqs.a: Because keyword-level scores tell you that your visibility changed, not why. A 'share of voice' number that drops doesn't show you that Perplexity started citing a competitor's comparison page or that ChatGPT pulled from a Reddit thread instead of your docs. Prompt-level data shows the actual answer and the specific prompt behind a citation, so you can see the cause and fix it. Independent reviewers flagged this as LLMrefs' main weakness, scoring it 2/5 on data accuracy and noting its most actionable view is buried in the UX.

LLMrefs defaults to weekly refreshes; monthly is common on lighter usage, and daily updates are available but require configuration. Reviewers consider the default cadence slow for fast-moving categories (GenerateMore scored freshness 2/5). Separately, like any parsing-based tracker, its citation parsers can temporarily break when OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google change response formatting, which can cause gaps until they're updated. For fast iteration, an on-demand audit like AEOeye's re-queries engines when you run it.

faqs.q: Which LLMrefs alternative is right for my budget?
faqs.a: For free and instant, start with AEOeye. For the cheapest paid prompt monitoring, Otterly.ai begins around $29/month. For a fast, clean mid-market tool, Peec AI starts near €89/month. For enterprise depth with deep historical analytics, Profound runs around $499/month. And if you want AI visibility alongside traditional SEO rank tracking in one tool, Nightwatch combines roughly $32/month SEO with a ~$99/month AI add-on. Match the tool to whether you optimize for price, speed, depth, or SEO integration.
